It is indispensable only with a whale that is a stubborn runner; its great feature and fact is the wonderful distance to which the long lance is accurately thrown from a violently rocking, jerking boat racing ahead at full speed. Strange as it may seem, this is exactly the case with the whale, who systematically lives, at intervals, his full hour and more (when at the bottom) without drawing a single breath or inhaling so much as a particle of air in any way; for remember, he has no gills. Between his ribs and on each side of his spine he is supplied with a remarkable, intricate Cretan labyrinth of vermicelli-like vessels, and when he leaves the surface these vessels are completely swollen with oxygenated blood.
